newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Sarajevans told not to peek at Pope.
newsitem.headline: Sarajevans told not to peek at Pope.

text.p: Bosnian police are leaving nothing to chance as they prepare for Pope John Paul's weekend visit to Sarajevo.
Policemen made housecalls on Thursday to tell city residents they should not even approach their windows while the Pope passes through town during his visit on Saturday and Sunday.
"I was told not to look through my windows for two days," an elderly woman living in a sixth-floor flat.
"I'm not sure when the two-day period begins, so I'll actually stop looking through my windows from tomorow on," she said.
The woman lives next door to Kosevo soccer stadium where some 40,000 people are expected to attend a Papal mass.
Sarajevans living in flats overlooking any street which might be used by the Pope during his tour were told to stay away from windows and not to touch their curtains, they said.

Policemen in uniform and plainclothes combed neighbourhoods around Kosevo stadium, going from flat to flat to inform people of the no-peek rules: "Do not approach the windows and don't touch the curtains".

Bosnian authorities are deploying thousands of policemen to protect the 76-year-old Pontiff. The Pope was forced to cancel a planned visit during the 1992-1995 Bosnian conflict after Serb forces beseiging the city refused to offer security guarantees.
This time, the Pope was invited to come to Sarajevo by Bosnia's collective presidency, a body which also includes a Serb member, Momcilo Krajisnik.
A wave of tit-for-tat bombing attacks on Roman Catholic churches and Islamic mosques that began in February has raised concerns about the Pope's safety.
Around the soccer stadium, a police tow truck was busy removing cars of shoppers who had parked near an outdoor market.
"You'd better go get your groceries today, because the market will be closed from Friday," the woman said.
